findings.note: Dead sub-assertion, verified by mutation. machine_test.go:74 joins two negated predicates with && where || was meant: `if !strings.HasPrefix(w, "WORKFLOW_WARNING") && !strings.Contains(w, "loop_without_clean_exit")`. It can only fail when BOTH are false, so once the prefix matches the atom substring is never checked. Rewriting it to || fails immediately with `warnings: [WORKFLOW_WARNING]` -- the Snapshot.Warnings entry is exactly the code string, because run/fold.go:198 folds only p.Code into Snapshot.Warnings. So the test asserts a property (the warning names loop_without_clean_exit) that the value it inspects can never carry, and the machine could propagate any WORKFLOW_WARNING body undetected. The atom text is only asserted in internal/fsm/workflow/workflow_test.go:355, never on the machine's propagation path.

findings.note: Bound assertion that can never fire. machine_test.go:799 claims `an all of 32 long-named cmd atoms yields a >1 KB name; it is capped, never a store rejection`, but the check at line 823 is `len(r.StopReason) > run.MaxShort+run.MaxText+8` == 5128, while the observed StopReason is 1118 and the fully uncapped value would still only be ~1250. Mutation confirms the safety net is elsewhere: removing run.CapText(r.Atom, run.MaxShort) at machine.go:775 fails the test with ERR_APPEND_REJECTED / ERR_AUDIT_INVALID (oversize) -- i.e. precisely the store rejection the comment says will not happen -- never via this length bound. The assertion should pin the atom at MaxShort.

findings.note: The test locks in a mislabeled error code. machine_test.go:1110 asserts that record data `nope` (invalid JSON, not oversized) returns CodeRecordTooLarge; machine.go:1010 indeed returns errs.E(CodeRecordTooLarge, "record data must be valid JSON") -- an error whose code contradicts its own message. docs/specs/2026-08-27-metareview-0.9.0-fsm-core.md:388 ties ERR_RECORD_TOO_LARGE to `Data <= MaxPayload - 128` only, so nothing in the spec sanctions reusing it for a parse failure. Either the spec should name this case or the code needs a distinct one; the test currently freezes the ambiguity.
